items.title: Evolution of Industrial Policy (1948 → 1956 → 1991)
items.body:
## The three landmark resolutions

- **IPR 1948** — India's **first** industrial policy; established a **mixed economy** with the state entering key industries while leaving room for private enterprise.
- **IPR 1956** — the **'economic constitution of India'**, framed to give effect to the **socialist pattern of society** and the **Second Five Year Plan** (Mahalanobis model). It classified industries into three schedules:

| Schedule | Nature | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| A (17 industries) | State exclusively responsible | Arms, atomic energy, railways |
| B | State + private together | Aluminium, machine tools, fertilisers |
| C | Left to the private sector | All remaining industries |

- **New Industrial Policy 1991** — the **liberalisation** turning point (part of LPG reforms): **abolished industrial licensing** except for a short list, **reduced public-sector reserved industries** from 17 to 8, opened the economy to **FDI**, and diluted the **MRTP Act** (later replaced by the **Competition Act, 2002**).

## Where reservation stands now
- Reserved for the public sector: **17 (1956) → 8 (1991) → 2 today** (atomic energy and railway operations).
keyPoints: IPR 1948 was India's first industrial policy and set up a mixed economy.
IPR 1956 — the 'economic constitution of India' — created Schedule A (17 state-exclusive industries), B and C, tied to the Second Plan.
The New Industrial Policy 1991 abolished most industrial licensing and launched liberalisation.
1991 reduced public-sector reserved industries from 17 to 8; today only 2 remain (atomic energy, railway operations).
The MRTP Act was replaced by the Competition Act, 2002 (CCI operational 2009).
items.mnemonic: Policy years '48-56-91' = Foundation (mixed economy) → Public-sector dominance → Liberalisation.
items.source: NCERT Indian Economic Development; DPIIT industrial policy history

items.title: Classification of Industries
items.body:
## By activity
- **Primary** — extraction/harvesting of nature's resources (agriculture, mining, forestry, fishing).
- **Secondary** — processing and manufacturing (steel, cement, textiles, automobiles, construction).
- **Tertiary** — services (banking, insurance, healthcare, transport, tourism).
- **Quaternary** — knowledge-based services (IT, R&D, consultancy).

## By ownership
- **Private sector** (Reliance, Tata), **Public sector** (IOC, BHEL), **Joint sector** (Maruti Suzuki, originally a govt–Suzuki JV), **Cooperative sector** (Amul, IFFCO).

## By product type
- **Consumer goods** (final use), **Capital goods** (machinery for other industries), **Intermediate goods** (inputs such as steel and chemicals).

## By scale
- **Small-scale** (low capital, labour-intensive) and **large-scale** (high capital, mass production).
keyPoints: By activity: primary (extraction), secondary (manufacturing), tertiary (services), quaternary (knowledge/R&D).
By ownership: private, public, joint (e.g. Maruti Suzuki) and cooperative (e.g. Amul, IFFCO).
By product: consumer goods, capital goods (machinery for other industries), intermediate goods.
Capital goods industries supply the machinery and equipment used by other industries.
items.source: local APPSC GK PDF — Indian Industries (classification)

items.title: Public Sector Enterprises & the Ratna Classification
items.body:
## Objectives of PSEs
- Accelerate growth in **critical sectors**, promote **balanced regional development**, generate **employment**, mobilise resources, retain control over **strategic sectors** (defence, energy, transport), and stabilise prices.

## Three organisational types
| Type | Feature | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Departmental undertaking | Run by a ministry; no separate legal identity | Indian Railways, India Post |
| Statutory corporation | Created by a special Act of Parliament | LIC, ONGC (originally) |
| Government company | Registered under the Companies Act; govt holds ≥51% | SAIL, BHEL, NTPC |

## Ratna status (autonomy grades)
- **Maharatna** (created 2010) — largest autonomy; invest up to 15% of net worth (cap ₹5,000 cr) without approval. Criteria: prior Navratna status, net worth ≥ ₹15,000 cr, turnover ≥ ₹25,000 cr, net profit ≥ ₹5,000 cr (3-yr averages).
- **Navratna** — invest up to ₹1,000 cr without approval; needs Miniratna status + score ≥ 60/100.
- **Miniratna Category-I & II** — lower autonomy for profit-making CPSEs.
- As of **2025: 14 Maharatnas, 26 Navratnas, 65 Miniratnas**.
keyPoints: PSEs aim at growth in critical sectors, balanced regional development, employment and control of strategic sectors.
Three types: departmental undertaking (Railways), statutory corporation (LIC), government company (SAIL, ≥51% govt).
Maharatna (created 2010): prior Navratna status, net worth ≥ ₹15,000 cr, turnover ≥ ₹25,000 cr, net profit ≥ ₹5,000 cr.
Maharatna can invest up to 15% of net worth (cap ₹5,000 cr) without government approval.
As of 2025 there are 14 Maharatnas, 26 Navratnas and 65 Miniratnas.
items.mnemonic: Autonomy ladder: Miniratna → Navratna → Maharatna (small to great jewel).
items.source: local APPSC GK PDF — Public Sector Enterprises; DPE guidelines 2025

items.title: MSMEs, Industrial Sickness & the IBC
items.body:
## MSME classification (composite: investment + turnover)
The **2020** reform (Atmanirbhar Bharat) merged the manufacturing/service distinction and adopted a composite criterion; limits were **enhanced with effect from 1 April 2025**:

| Class (from 1 Apr 2025) | Investment | Turnover |
|---|---|---|
| Micro | ≤ ₹2.5 cr | ≤ ₹10 cr |
| Small | ≤ ₹25 cr | ≤ ₹100 cr |
| Medium | ≤ ₹125 cr | ≤ ₹500 cr |

## Significance & problems
- MSMEs contribute about **30% of GDP** and nearly **half of exports**, and are the second-largest employer after agriculture.
- Common problems: **inadequate/costly credit, delayed payments, obsolete technology, marketing and infrastructure gaps**.

## Industrial sickness & the IBC
- **Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 (IBC)** provides a **time-bound** resolution of corporate distress, replacing the older **SICA/BIFR** sickness mechanism.
- Adjudicated by the **NCLT**; a **pre-packaged** insolvency route was added for MSMEs in 2021.
keyPoints: MSME uses a composite investment-plus-turnover criterion (2020), with no manufacturing/service distinction.
From 1 Apr 2025: Micro ≤ ₹2.5cr/₹10cr, Small ≤ ₹25cr/₹100cr, Medium ≤ ₹125cr/₹500cr (investment/turnover).
MSMEs contribute ~30% of GDP and nearly half of exports; key problems are credit shortage and delayed payments.
The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 gives a time-bound resolution and replaced SICA/BIFR.
IBC cases for companies are adjudicated by the NCLT.
items.source: Ministry of MSME; Union Budget 2025-26; IBC 2016 / IBBI

items.title: Make in India, PLI & Startup/Standup India
items.body:
## Make in India (25 September 2014)
- Aims to make India a **global manufacturing hub**; originally **25 sectors**; slogan **'Zero Defect, Zero Effect'**; targets raising **manufacturing to ~25% of GDP**.

## Production Linked Incentive (PLI, from 2020)
- Pays incentives as a **percentage of incremental sales** of goods **manufactured in India**.
- Covers **14 sectors** (mobile/electronics, pharma, auto & components, telecom, textiles, food processing, solar PV, etc.) with a total outlay of about **₹1.97 lakh crore**; aims to cut import dependence.

## Startup India & Standup India (both 2016)
- **Startup India** — DPIIT recognition, tax benefits, easier compliance, a **Fund of Funds** to nurture innovation-based startups.
- **Standup India** — facilitates bank loans of **₹10 lakh–₹1 crore** for at least one **SC/ST** and one **woman** entrepreneur per bank branch for a greenfield enterprise.

## Eight Core Industries & IIP
- Eight core: **Coal, Crude Oil, Natural Gas, Refinery Products, Fertilizers, Steel, Cement, Electricity** — about **40.27% weight** in the **Index of Industrial Production (IIP)** (base year 2011-12).
keyPoints: Make in India launched 25 Sep 2014, 25 sectors, 'Zero Defect Zero Effect', targets ~25% manufacturing GDP share.
PLI (2020) rewards incremental domestic sales across 14 sectors, outlay ~₹1.97 lakh crore.
Startup India (2016) offers DPIIT recognition, tax breaks and a Fund of Funds.
Standup India (2016) funds ₹10 lakh–₹1 crore loans for SC/ST and women entrepreneurs.
Eight Core Industries carry ~40.27% weight in the IIP (base 2011-12): coal, crude oil, natural gas, refinery, fertilizers, steel, cement, electricity.
items.mnemonic: Core-8: 'Come Come, Not Really For Some Cool Energy' — Coal, Crude oil, Natural gas, Refinery, Fertilizers, Steel, Cement, Electricity.
items.source: DPIIT — Make in India, PLI, Startup India; DFS — Standup India; Office of Economic Adviser (IIP)

items.title: Industrial Corridors, Labour Codes & the AP Angle
items.body:
## Industrial infrastructure
- **SEZ** — duty-free enclave treated as foreign territory for trade/tariffs (**SEZ Act, 2005**).
- **NIMZ** — large integrated industrial township under the **National Manufacturing Policy, 2011**.
- **Corridors** — **DMIC** (Delhi-Mumbai, the first flagship corridor), CBIC, Amritsar-Kolkata, and the **East Coast Economic Corridor (ECEC)**.

## Four labour codes (implemented 2025)
- Consolidate **29 central labour laws** into **four codes**: **Code on Wages, 2019**; **Industrial Relations Code, 2020**; **Code on Social Security, 2020**; **Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020**.
- Came **into force on 21 November 2025**; extend social security to **gig and platform workers** and standardise the wage definition.

## Andhra Pradesh angle
- **VCIC (Visakhapatnam-Chennai Industrial Corridor)** — the **first phase of the ECEC**, India's **first coastal economic corridor**; the **ADB** is the lead development partner; ~800 km through several AP districts, aligned with the **Golden Quadrilateral** and supporting the **Act East Policy**.
- The **AP Industrial Development Policy** promotes investment nodes such as **Sri City** (multi-product SEZ), **Kopparthi (Kadapa)** and **Orvakal (Kurnool)**; AP is strong in ports (Visakhapatnam), pharma and food processing.
keyPoints: SEZs (SEZ Act 2005) are duty-free enclaves; NIMZs are integrated townships under the National Manufacturing Policy 2011.
DMIC (Delhi-Mumbai) was India's first flagship industrial corridor.
Four labour codes consolidate 29 central laws: Wages (2019), Industrial Relations, Social Security, OSH (all 2020).
The four labour codes came into force on 21 November 2025 and cover gig/platform workers.
VCIC is the first phase of the East Coast Economic Corridor (India's first coastal corridor), with ADB as lead partner, running through AP.
AP investment nodes include Sri City, Kopparthi (Kadapa) and Orvakal (Kurnool).
items.source: DPIIT/NICDC; Ministry of Labour & Employment (labour codes, 21 Nov 2025); ADB / Government of Andhra Pradesh — VCIC

items.title: Exam-Precision: Data Agencies, Standards Marks & Enterprise-Finance Schemes
items.body:
## Who compiles what?

| Body | Function (PYQ trigger) |
|---|---|
| **Labour Bureau** (attached office, Min. of Labour & Employment) | Compiles data on **industrial disputes, closures, retrenchments and lay-offs** in factories; also CPI-IW. NOT the CSO/DPIIT |
| **Coal Controller's Organization (CCO)** | A major source of **coal statistics**; monitors **captive coal/lignite block** development; hears objections to acquisition of coal-bearing areas. It does **NOT** guarantee timely delivery of coal to end-users |
| **NSO/MoSPI** | Compiles the **Index of Industrial Production (IIP)** |

## Standards marks

- **BIS ISI mark** is **mandatory** for products such as **automotive tyres and tubes**.
- **AGMARK** is issued by the **Directorate of Marketing & Inspection (DMI), Ministry of Agriculture** - **NOT** by the FAO.

## Eight Core Industries - weights

Among the eight infrastructure sectors, **Electricity** carries the **highest weight** (~19.85%), ahead of Steel and Coal. (In the overall composite the largest single weight is Refinery Products, but of the eight sectors listed in exams Electricity tops.) The eight together are ~40.27% of the IIP.

## Enterprise-finance & turnaround schemes

| Scheme | Purpose |
|---|---|
| **PM MUDRA Yojana (2015)** | Bring **small/micro entrepreneurs into the formal financial system** (Shishu/Kishore/Tarun) |
| **Stand Up India** | Entrepreneurship among **SC/ST & women**; **refinance via SIDBI** |
| **UDAY (2015)** | **Financial turnaround of power distribution companies (DISCOMs)** |
| **S4A (2016)** | **RBI** scheme to rework the financial structure of large corporates in genuine difficulty |
| **Small Finance Banks** | Credit to **small business units and small & marginal farmers** (financial inclusion) |
keyPoints: The Labour Bureau compiles data on industrial disputes, closures, retrenchments and lay-offs (not the CSO or DPIIT).
The Coal Controller's Organization is a major source of coal statistics and monitors captive coal/lignite block development.
The BIS ISI mark is mandatory for automotive tyres and tubes; AGMARK is issued by the Directorate of Marketing & Inspection (Ministry of Agriculture), not the FAO.
Among the Eight Core Industries, Electricity carries the highest weight; the eight together are about 40.27% of the IIP.
PM MUDRA formalises micro-entrepreneurs; Stand Up India (SC/ST & women) is refinanced through SIDBI; UDAY revives DISCOMs; S4A is an RBI stressed-asset scheme.
Small Finance Banks provide credit to small business units and small & marginal farmers.
items.source: PIB; RBI; Ministry of Labour (Labour Bureau); Ministry of Coal (CCO); BIS; UPSC PYQ pattern
